references.text: Jacob commands his household to remove the foreign gods that were among them, just as Joshua does here.
The first commandment forbids having other gods, which is the core of Joshua's exhortation to remove foreign gods.
The command to love the Lord with all one's heart connects to Joshua's call to turn the heart to the Lord.
Samuel gives Israel the same exhortation to remove foreign gods and turn their hearts to the Lord alone.
Israel removes the foreign gods from among them, in obedience to similar exhortations.
A warning against letting the heart be led astray to worship other gods, which is the background for Joshua's exhortation.
A prayer that God would incline the heart toward His testimonies, the same theme of the heart's direction toward God.
The promise that God will write His law on hearts, related to turning the heart to the Lord.
Ezekiel exhorts Israel to turn away from idols, the same theme as in Joshua.
John exhorts believers to keep themselves from idols, echoing Joshua's exhortation.
